entries.review_note: Hirata finds the concealed underwear while searching Kiyotaka and chooses private inquiry rather than accusation.
Karuizawa and Horikita dispute gendered restrictions; their positions are not universal personal ethics.
Sakura speaks up for Kiyotaka and is rebuffed by Karuizawa; courage with limited social success.
Class D formally separates boys' and girls' accommodations after suspicion, an episode-specific outcome.
Kiyotaka suspects Ibuki planted underwear but does not yet have an admitted fact at this stage.
Fans in girls' camp reveal extra spending; source does not give complete cumulative equipment accounts.
Suzune's continuing fever visibly reduces her performance; no clinical diagnosis is established.
Yamauchi smears mud on Suzune and she throws him; this is immediate reaction under illness.
Horikita privately reports leader keycard missing and asks Kiyotaka because she trusts him.
An unidentified party burns the test manual; no eyewitness establishes the arsonist.
Hirata dissociates under crisis and mutters about earlier trouble; exact past incident unknown here.
Feverish Suzune follows suspected Ibuki into heavy rain; her suspicion is not all confirmed yet.
Ibuki launches physical attack as Suzune questions her; health affects the response.
Ill Suzune fights Ibuki but collapses, giving no sound healthy-versus-healthy ranking.
Ibuki's own perspective confirms covert mission, failed camera, planted slap and later return of keycard.
Ryūen and Katsuragi directly inspect stolen leader card; their knowledge arises at meeting, not earlier.
Katsuragi agrees to Class A–C alliance; full consideration and contract terms remain partly undisclosed.
Kiyotaka arrives after Ibuki leaves and attends unconscious Suzune; discovery chronology is storm-specific.
Kiyotaka's fall while carrying Suzune exhibits bounded protective response and risk, not invulnerability.
Kiyotaka privately describes peers as tools and winning as overriding aim; others cannot access his monologue.
He reaches ship with Suzune near 19:58 yet is out for 20:00 camp roll call, and returns leader card.
He expects thirty-point medical retirement and five-point personal absence; calculation in his own narration.
Hirata reports 125 provisional points before leader-guess effects; not Class D final result.
Mashima says test concluded and permits relaxation while teachers count final class results.
Published exam scores: C 0, A 120, B 140, D 225; direct public announcement.
Class D celebrates surprise rank; Ryūen's expectations fail in this result, not every strategy.
Teacher reports family-linked pressure over Kiyotaka; outside party's authority is unproved.
Chabashira frames choices through Icarus; rhetoric alone cannot force student intent.
Kiyotaka retrospectively interprets Class A cave-card scene; partly his later hypothesis.
Kiyotaka confirms he replaced Suzune as leader after medical retirement; secret was not Class D's earlier shared knowledge.
He invokes justified replacement exception; do not encode unlimited leader mutations.
He infers Ibuki's covert agenda using behavior and rival Kaneda, but not every observation was public.
Economics of Class A–C arrangement are partly Kiyotaka's intuition; a basic alliance is separately depicted through Ibuki.
Kiyotaka privately ascribes intervention to Chabashira's earlier pressure, not a certainty accessible to Suzune.
He offers continuing help conditional on Suzune respecting his privacy; she accepts at scene.
Sakayanagi's absence is discussed by Ichinose/Kanzaki, without all class faction authority proved.
Kaneda is observed helping in B camp, while Kiyotaka later calls him Ryūen's spy; late attribution not contemporaneous B knowledge.
